title: Berlin Monthly Ticket - Quick Summary
items: **The Berlin-only monthly ticket costs more than the national one.** Checked on 17 September 2026: a **VBB Umweltkarte AB is 81.30 euros** a month on a subscription, and the **Deutschlandticket is 63 euros** and is valid on every local and regional service in Germany. Buying the same Berlin AB card month by month without a contract costs **113 euros**, which is **50 euros a month, 600 a year**, for a smaller map.

**Sixteen rides is the line.** At the **4.00 euro AB single fare**, the Deutschlandticket pays for itself on your sixteenth ride of the month, which is eight return journeys. On **4-Fahrten-Karten at 3.10 euros a ride** the crossing point moves to twenty-one. The Umweltkarte AB needs twenty-one single rides to break even, the contract-free 113 euro version needs twenty-nine.

**The Umweltkarte buys two specific things.** It is **transferable**, so a flatmate or partner can take it while you are away, and from **20:00 on weekdays until 03:00**, plus all day Saturday, Sunday, public holidays, 24 and 31 December, it carries **up to four people of whom only one may be over 14**. The Deutschlandticket is personal and carries nobody.

**Two adults, one card, is where it wins.** Two separate Deutschlandtickets cost **126 euros** a month. If one of you travels in the daytime and the other mostly in the evenings and at weekends, a single transferable Umweltkarte AB at 81.30 covers both and saves **44.70 euros a month**. Two daytime commuters cannot share one card, and then two Deutschlandtickets win.

**Zone C is the other big gap.** BER and Potsdam are both in zone C, so an AB card stops short of them. An **Umweltkarte ABC is 103.30 euros**; the Deutschlandticket reaches both plus every RE and RB out of Berlin for 63. That is **40.30 euros a month, 483.60 a year**, for the smaller ticket.

**No season ticket carries your bike.** A **Monatskarte Fahrrad is 14.60 euros for AB, 18.20 for ABC**, it is transferable, and it only works alongside a valid main ticket. Bikes travel in marked carriages when there is room, never on a bus. **ICE, IC and EC** always need a separate ticket too.

**Check the cheaper doors before you buy.** A **Deutschlandticket Job** through a participating employer costs at most **44.10 euros**, which is 226.80 a year less. **Berlin-Ticket S is 27.50 euros** for people on benefits with proof. Both tickets cancel monthly, and the deadline is the **10th of the month** for the end of that month.
